summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (248 ft square, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise, rebuilt by Perkins&Will and Plant Construction as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. Held on a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease; nearly 90% leased by August 2026, with General Catalyst taking the whole third floor.

milestones.text: Built by U.S. Navy personnel as Plate Shop No. 2, the central building of the New Yard on ground leveled from Irish Hill
Listed as a contributing resource of the Union Iron Works Historic District

DDA terms approved: a vertical developer affiliate must take a 66-year lease of Building 12 within a year after completion of the public improvements for Parcel E2, base rent $1/year, participation rent 3.5% of modified gross income from year 31 after TCO, and seek historic tax credits
Phase 1 groundbreaking: the Port describes Building 12 as a 120,000 sq ft industrial hub to be elevated 9 feet for sea-level-rise protection

Building 15 lifted about nine feet and moved 200 ft to its permanent position over the new 22nd Street to allow work on Building 12; Building 12 itself lifted (10 ft per the architect, 12 ft per ENR and the contractor) on more than 200 hydraulic jacks over four weeks
Perkins&Will describes the roof-first construction sequence and the lift to address a 100-year sea-level projection
Building 12 receives its temporary certificate of occupancy; The City Canvas: A Paint the Void Retrospective (January 22-30, 2022) draws close to 6,000 attendees
ENR California Award of Merit, Renovation/Restoration
Brookfield reported to have spent $237.4 million on Phase 1, including infrastructure, roads and the Building 12 restoration; Building 12 hosted the Oracle NetSuite Open squash tournament
Leases signed in fall 2022 with Standard Deviant Brewing and Breadbelly (in discussions since March 2020)

Seven maker and food tenants announced (Standard Deviant, Breadbelly, Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, and a shared studio for Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis), about 20,000 sq ft in total, leases of three to ten years
Building 12 Preview Party (August 2-3, 2024) with all Building 12 tenants, Bandaloop and the Noonan Artists
Standard Deviant Brewing's taproom opens (reported open within two weeks before June 25, 2025; the Port's June 2025 deck shows it open)
General Catalyst signs a 70,000 sq ft office lease for the entire third floor; Monograph Capital had leased in 2024
Port reports Building 12 nearly 90% leased, with two venture capital firms taking the entire third-floor office space
OTC alterations permit M1230687 issued to add the address 1070 Maryland St to APN 4110-010 at Pier 70 Building 12, at the request of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development

facts.value: 1070 Maryland St (Brookfield's Building 12 page; the 2023 Real Deal report gives 180 Maryland Street)

Nabih Youssef Associates; shoring design Degenkolb Engineers; lifting contractor Bigge Crane & Rigging; civil BKF; MEP Point Energy Innovations; enclosure RDH
248 ft 2 in by 242 ft 2 in by 59 ft 6 in tall; Aiken roof with five glazed monitors

118,890 over two floors historically (NRHP); 230,000 sq ft after adaptive reuse per the architect (contractor: 220,000 sq ft, 60,000 sq ft main warehouse plus a 45,000 sq ft mezzanine and 60,000 sq ft of office); about 200,000 sq ft per the 2026 Real Deal report
Ground-floor market hall with large-scale production and retail, second-floor maker and artisan studios, third-floor office
Structure raised approximately 10 feet (architect) / 12 feet (ENR, contractor) to sit above 100-year sea-level-rise projections; the Port's 2018 release said 9 feet
66 years from the Port at $1/year base rent with participation rent from year 31 (DDA terms)

Standard Deviant Brewing, Breadbelly, Sven Ceramics, Bay Padel, The Plenary Co., Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis; two venture capital firms on the third floor (General Catalyst and Monograph Capital)
ENR California Best Projects Award of Merit 2022; AIA California Honor Award 2024; AIA San Francisco Honor Award for adaptive reuse 2024; WAN Silver 2023 (architect's list)
Plate shop and mold loft for hull construction at Slips 5-8; vacant at the time of the 2013 nomination

open_questions: Construction cost of the Building 12 rehabilitation itself: not stated anywhere; only the $237.4M Phase 1 total (Oct 2022) and the $150M infrastructure Notice of Completion figure exist.
Whether the 66-year Building 12 lease has been executed, and its date: the DDA sets the trigger, but no Port Commission lease approval for Building 12 was found on 2018-2026 agendas.
The lift height is given as 9 ft (Port, 2018), 10 ft (Perkins&Will) and 12 ft (ENR, Plant); square footage as 200,000-230,000 depending on source.
The address appears as 1070 Maryland Street (Brookfield, 2026 reports) and 180 Maryland Street (2023 Real Deal report); status.csv uses 1070.
No 'now' photograph with a stated license was found; the D4D images hosted here pre-date the rehabilitation.

The four D4D-credited photographs of Building 12 (building12.jpg, building12_corrugated.jpg, building12_interior.jpg, building12_roof.jpg) are straight architectural photographs taken in 2017, not scanned drawings or plans; `kind: document` fits the schema's 'page from a source document' reading but they may read better as `before` (pre-rehabilitation condition) if the record's kind taxonomy is revisited.
